extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies and foreign private issuers), securities lawyers, compliance officers, assurance providers, and investors
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidance implementing the SEC's final climate-related disclosure requirements, including scope, timing/phase-in by filer type, assurance, structured data tagging, and legal treatment of disclosures (filed vs furnished). Intended to guide registrants and their advisors in preparing SEC filings to satisfy the new climate-related disclosure regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of climate-related disclosures as filed
rubrics_metrics.description: As proposed, the climate-related disclosures provided pursuant to the final rules will be treated as filed. Climate-related disclosures will therefore be subject to potential liability pursuant to Exchange Act section 18 and, if included or otherwise incorporated by reference into a Securities Act registration statement, Securities Act section 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: treating disclosures as filed will help promote accuracy and consistency and subjects them to the same liability as other business or financial information. Acknowledge commenters' concerns about evolving methodologies; mitigation measures include limiting scope of GHG requirements, revising certain provisions (materiality conditions), providing a PSLRA safe harbor, and transition periods based on filer status and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the scope of the GHG emissions disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission modified the proposal by limiting the scope of the GHG emissions disclosure requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: mitigate concerns about complexity and evolving nature of GHG measurement. Implementation detail elsewhere in the rules: GHG emissions disclosure requirements will apply only with respect to LAFs and AFs (other than SRCs and EGCs) according to the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality-limited disclosures for strategy, targets/goals, and climate-related metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Revising several provisions regarding the impacts of climate-related risks on strategy, targets and goals, and climate-related metrics so that registrants will only be required to provide the disclosures in certain circumstances, such as when material to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These revisions narrow mandatory disclosure to information that is material; the rules acknowledge that not all registrants will have applicable information (e.g., governance disclosures only required to the extent registrant has responsive information).

rubrics_metrics.name: PSLRA safe harbor for certain climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing an additional PSLRA safe harbor for several types of climate-related disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to mitigate litigation risk concerns raised by commenters. The safe harbor applies to certain forward-looking climate-related statements as specified in the rules (see full text for enumerated categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition period based on filer status and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing registrants with a transition period based on filer status and the content of the required information to afford registrants additional time to prepare to provide the climate-related disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition periods are staggered by filer type (LAF, AF, NAF, SRC, EGC) and by the particular disclosure or assurance requirement; the Commission provided examples illustrating which fiscal years (FYB) apply to different filers and disclosure types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased in compliance dates by registrant type (LAF, AF, NAF, SRC, EGC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting delayed and staggered compliance dates for the final rules that vary according to the filing status of the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules include detailed compliance tables showing: disclosure and financial statement effects audit dates; GHG emissions/assurance dates; and structured data (electronic tagging) dates. Rationale: many LAFs already collect/disclose climate information; non-LAFs receive additional time to implement systems, controls, and processes. Examples: LAFs FYB 2025 for most disclosures; AFs FYB 2026; SRCs/EGCs/NAFs FYB 2027 (see tables for specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased assurance requirements for GHG emissions (limited and reasonable assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules set separate phased-in compliance dates for assurance over GHG emissions disclosures, with limited assurance required at a later date and reasonable assurance at a still-later date for certain filers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example for LAFs: Scopes 1 and 2 disclosure required FYB 2026; limited assurance required FYB 2029; reasonable assurance required FYB 2033. For some filer categories (e.g., some SRCs, EGCs), assurance requirements may be N/A. See compliance tables for each registrant type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate compliance date for structured data (electronic tagging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting a separate compliance date for the structured data (electronic tagging) requirements of the final rules that is one year following the earliest compliance date (which applies to LAFs) under the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: improve quality of structured data. LAFs will not be required to comply with structured data at initial climate disclosure compliance (FYB 2025) but will be required at FYB 2026; AFs, SRCs, EGCs, and NAFs have corresponding later dates tied to their initial compliance dates. Certain items (see next metric) are tagged at initial compliance with those provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured data tagging required at initial compliance for specific items
rubrics_metrics.description: Tagging of disclosures provided in response to Item 1502(d)(2), Item 1502(e)(2), Item 1504(c)(2), Item 1505, and Item 1506 will be required at the time of initial compliance with these provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although overall structured data compliance is phased, certain specified items will require inline XBRL tagging when a registrant first becomes subject to those particular provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of the final rules' provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission considers the provisions of the final rules to be severable to the fullest extent permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts of the regulation are held invalid, the Commission intends that such invalidity shall not affect other provisions capable of operating independently. Examples of independent portions: (1) climate-related risk disclosures, (2) targets and goals disclosures, (3) GHG emissions disclosures and assurance, and (4) Article 14 financial statement disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to registration statements and periodic reports; incorporation by reference permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure requirements being adopted will apply to Securities Act and Exchange Act registration statements as well as Exchange Act annual and quarterly reports; in many cases registrants will be able to meet these requirements by incorporating by reference from their periodic reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In registration statements, compliance is required beginning in any registration statement that is required to include financial information for the full fiscal year indicated in the compliance tables. Registrants without prior periodic reports (e.g., IPO S-1/F-1 filers) cannot incorporate by reference and therefore must include required disclosures directly in the offering document when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for Canadian MJDS filers (Form 40-F)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules will affect both domestic registrants and foreign private issuers, but will not apply to Canadian registrants that use the MJDS and file their Exchange Act registration statements and annual reports on Form 40-F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This carve-out recognizes existing bilateral filing frameworks; other foreign private issuers filing on Form 20-F remain within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic analysis: weigh benefits, costs, and effects on efficiency/competition/capital formation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission analyzes expected economic effects of the final rules relative to the baseline, including benefits, costs, and the effects on efficiency, competition, and capital formation; quantifies where possible and provides qualitative assessment where quantification is not practical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed/anticipated benefits include more consistent, comparable, reliable disclosures enabling better investor decisions, reduced information asymmetry, lower risk premia, and improved stock liquidity. Costs include compliance burdens (varying by filer status and existing practices), litigation risk, and potential disclosure of proprietary information; third parties (market participants, customers, suppliers) could face reduced demand or higher input prices. The rules acknowledge limitations in available empirical evidence for some quantifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of affected parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected parties include registrants subject to the forms' disclosure requirements, consumers of climate-related information (investors, analysts, market participants), and third-party service providers such as assurance providers and ratings providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis covers domestic registrants and foreign private issuers (with an estimated count of registrants by filer type), and notes how many registrants may already be subject to overlapping state, federal, or international requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing SEC disclosure provisions may already encompass climate-related risks (Item 101/103/105/303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing disclosure requirements (Item 101 Description of Business, Item 103 Legal Proceedings, Item 105 Risk Factors, Item 303 Management's Discussion & Analysis) can encompass climate-related risk but have not produced consistent, comparable information about material climate-related impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2010 Guidance discussed this; the final rules are intended to standardize disclosures to better meet investor needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship and differences with EPA's GHGRP
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the GHGRP and the final rules both address reporting of GHGs, they have distinct goals and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences noted: (1) entities required to report may differ; (2) EPA requires emissions reporting only for U.S. facilities, while final rules are not limited to U.S. facilities; (3) EPA emissions data do not allow precise disaggregation across scopes for a registrant; (4) EPA does not require reporting of Scope 2 emissions. The SEC acknowledges overlap but explains distinct purposes (EPA for policymaking/registry; SEC for investor disclosure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with state and international climate-related reporting regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: State laws (e.g., NAIC survey, California SB 253 and SB 261) and international regimes (TCFD, ISSB, CSRD/ESRS) impose or will impose climate-related reporting obligations that may overlap or affect registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and international rules vary by scope, thresholds, methodologies, and timing. Some registrants may already be subject to these regimes and have systems/processes in place; the SEC considers these when setting compliance timing and scope. Examples: NAIC survey alignment with TCFD; California laws' thresholds and timing for Scopes 1/2/3; ISSB standards incorporate TCFD and align with GHG Protocol; CSRD phased implementation and possible overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased-in compliance for specified financial-impact disclosures (Item 1502(d)(2), 1502(e)(2), 1504(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing a further phased-in compliance date for the requirements to provide quantitative and qualitative disclosures about material expenditures and material impacts to financial estimates and assumptions required by Item 1502(d)(2), Item 1502(e)(2), and Item 1504(c)(2) until the fiscal year immediately following the fiscal year of the registrant's initial compliance date for subpart 1500 disclosures based on its filer status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses commenters' concerns that additional time is necessary for registrants to develop controls, processes, and system solutions to produce reliable financial-impact disclosures tied to climate risks.
